guard: the feed pump rejects private destinations, bounds remote bodies, isolates bad items, labels remote text as untrusted, and keeps agent control on a separate channel
why: M1 restores the malformed-date crash by carrying the raw RSS date into render. The date cell
requires the parsed item to omit that value, so render's defensive guard is not credited alone.
M2 removes the untrusted-data marker from the shipped message. The output cell drives render,
rather than searching source, and turns red on the message a real agent receives.
M3 disables private-address filtering. The address table contains loopback, link-local,
documentation and IPv6 cases plus public controls, so a predicate that always blocks or always
M4 removes redirect revalidation. A fake first response redirects from a public literal to the
metadata address; the test requires refusal before a second request is made.
M5 removes the streamed body cap. The cell drives a response with no content-length header, so
checking that header alone cannot satisfy it.
M6 puts feedkeeper back on the raw feed channel. The cell reads the persona and channel registry
that users actually spawn, and rejects the old authority path.
